Exercise 4: Push and pull

  1. Find an interesting AI/ML image and pull it docker pull jupyter/scipy-notebook

    Or run it directly: docker run jupyter/scipy-notebook

    Question: Suggested arguments for running this image?
    My suggestions:-p 10000:8888 -d
  2. Pushing your image This will require setting up a user that can push to whichever registry you want to push it to. Generally it would follow this structure: 
    
docker login <REGISTRY_HOST>:<REGISTRY_PORT>
docker tag <IMAGE_ID> <REGISTRY_HOST>:<REGISTRY_PORT>/<APPNAME>:<APPVERSION>
docker push <REGISTRY_HOST>:<REGISTRY_PORT>/<APPNAME>:<APPVERSION>

    An example would look like:

    
docker login repo.company.com:3456
docker tag 19fcc4aa71ba repo.company.com:3456/myapp:0.1
docker push repo.company.com:3456/myapp:0.1

    Or in our case with default Docker Hub:

    
docker login --username jeppetk
docker tag 90c46295c455 jeppetk/iris-train:initial
docker push jeppetk/iris-train
  3. What do the hashes represent when pushing/pulling? It's the different layers. This can be confirmed with the command docker inspect 90c46295c455

Next: Exercise 5 - Clean up
